podcast.title: Missed Pan Am Flight 103 (1988)
podcast.body: Johnny Lydon and his wife, Nora, narrowly missed Pan Am Flight 103 on December 21, 1988, which was later bombed over Lockerbie, Scotland. Delays caused by Nora taking too long to pack, a subsequent argument, and getting stuck in traffic on the way to Heathrow Airport meant they missed the flight by minutes, thus saving their lives. "Nora, his wife, took too long to pack. They had a big fight, which delayed them even more, and then they got stuck in traffic on the way to Heathrow. They missed their flight by minutes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Aggressive Dance Punk with Public Image Limited
podcast.body: After his time with the Sex Pistols, Johnny Lydon led Public Image Limited (PIL) in exploring a more aggressive form of dance punk. While still danceable, PIL's music had a distinct edge, described as "scary," "agitated," and "twitchy." "There was also a more aggressive version of this approach, led by Johnny Lydon's post-sex pistols band Public Image Limited."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Auditioning Michael Balzary (Flea) for PiL
podcast.body: In 1984, Johnny Lydon auditioned a young bass player from Los Angeles named Michael Balzary (later known as Flea) for Public Image Limited. Flea got the gig but chose instead to stick with his new band, the Red Hot Chili Peppers, which he was forming with his friend Anthony. "One of the people, Johnny auditioned for the band in 1984, was a young bass player from Los Angeles named Michael Ballzary."

podcast.title: Caregiver for Wife with Alzheimer's
podcast.body: Johnny Lydon is a dedicated caregiver for his wife, Nora, whom he affectionately calls "babby," as she battles Alzheimer's disease. His personal experience with childhood memory loss from meningitis allows him to deeply empathize with her condition and the challenges she faces, providing her with round-the-clock care. "He will also tell you about his wife Nora who he's caring for as she deals with Alzheimer's."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Childhood Meningitis
podcast.body: As a child, Johnny Lydon contracted a severe case of meningitis that left him in a coma for nearly a year. The lasting effects of this illness are credited with causing his distinctive stare. "Johnny Liden, who came down with a terrible case of meningitis as a kid, which left him comatose for nearly a year. The after effects give him that distinctive stare."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dark Music Contribution
podcast.body: Johnny Lydon's work with Public Image Limited was noted for its dark sound, contributing to the development of the Goth scene. "Johnny Lydon's public image limited was pretty dark, same with Killing Joke."

podcast.title: Post-Sex Pistols Musical Freedom
podcast.body: After leaving the Sex Pistols, Johnny Lydon gained the freedom to pursue his personal musical interests, which included a strong admiration for the German avant-garde group Can. This freedom allowed him to indulge in new musical directions with Public Image Limited. "And once he was out of the sex pistols, he was free to indulge in his musical whims."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Potential Eyesight Deterioration
podcast.body: In addition to the permanent curvature of his spine and his distinctive stare, Johnny Lydon lives with the possibility that his eyesight will progressively deteriorate into nothingness due to the long-term effects of his childhood spinal meningitis. "He was also left with a permanent curvature of the spine and that stare and the possibility that his eyesight will deteriorate into nothingness."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Profound Memory Loss and Identity Crisis
podcast.body: After being discharged from the hospital following his meningitis battle, Johnny Lydon suffered from severe memory loss that persisted for about four years, leaving him unable to recall his own name, his parents' names, or virtually anything from his past. He later reflected that this ordeal forced him to completely rebuild his identity, calling the meningitis "God's greatest gift" because it compelled him to discover who he truly was. "He couldn't remember his name or the name of his mom and dad."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Spinal Meningitis and Lasting Effects
podcast.body: Johnny Lydon contracted a severe case of spinal meningitis at the age of seven, an illness that left him with a permanent, intimidating stare and a lasting curvature of the spine. He spent an entire year at St. Anne's Hospital in London, enduring nausea, headaches, intermittent comas, hallucinations, and painful spinal taps, missing over a year of school. "It's the result of a terrible case of spinal men and gytus that he contracted when he was seven."

xref.title: Formation and Johnny Rotten's Audition (1975)
xref.body: In 1975, Malcolm McLaren, the former manager of The New York Dolls and co-proprietor of the "Sex" clothing shop at 430 King's Road in London's Chelsea area, sought to form a band as a living advertisement for his store. He liked the name "Pistols" for its dangerous connotation, thus "Sex Pistols." Malcolm was looking for a singer and was introduced to 19-year-old Johnny Lydon (later Johnny Rotten), who had green teeth and was spotted by Bernie Rhodes wearing a homemade "I hate Pink Floyd" t-shirt held together with safety pins. Despite Lydon's inability to sing, Malcolm had him audition by miming and "singing" Alice Cooper's "I'm 18" to a jukebox in the shop, which landed him the role. "So Malcolm got young John to audition, not caring if Johnny could actually sing a note, which he couldn't."

xref.title: Chaotic New York Concert (May 15, 1980)
xref.body: Public Image Limited (P.I.L.), led by Johnny Lydon (formerly Johnny Rotten), agreed to play two nights at the Ritz in New York for a $12,000 fee, despite internal squabbles, drug abuse, and money problems. The band was in no shape to play, lacking a drummer (the sixth one quit) and a bass player (who had just walked out). They quickly hired a 65-year-old jazz drummer from a Broadway music shop. Instead of performing live, P.I.L. pantomimed along to their records, hidden from the audience by a large screen with their silhouettes projected by bright white lights. The 1,500 people in the audience were kept waiting in the pouring rain for over an hour, then discovered the band wasn't playing, and Johnny Lydon began taunting and insulting the crowd. This led to a rain of garbage, a storming of the stage, and the destruction of all equipment, with the gig ending after just 25 minutes. "The gig was killed after just 25 minutes."

xref.title: Reunion After Nearly 17 Years (2009)
xref.body: The band's reunion was officially announced on September 7, 2009, meaning they had been apart for 16 years, 11 months, and 20 days since their last gig. The reunion featured Johnny Lydon out front, but with different musicians, essentially making it "Johnny's band." "The time between that last show and the reunion was 16 years, 11 months, and 20 days. I guess we should play something for Metal Box, shouldn't we?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Reunion Motivated by Album Anniversary and Personal Tragedy (2009)
xref.body: In the summer of 2009, Johnny Lydon decided to revive Public Image Limited. This decision was influenced by the 30th-anniversary re-release of their influential "Metal Box" album, and also by emotional factors: the loss of his father to cancer in 2008 and the recurrence of his brother's cancer. These events reminded him of his mother's death during PiL's active period, which had inspired their song "Death Disco," suggesting "unfinished business." "The actual announcement came out on September the 7th of 2009. That was one reason. Another was a little more emotional."

xref.title: Anti-Rock Band Ambition
xref.body: Johnny Lydon deliberately aimed to create an "anti-rock band" after the Sex Pistols, moving away from punk's guitars and traditional rock's riffage. "Public Image Limited, Johnny Lydon's band after the Sex Pistols, was also unconventional in its own way. Johnny deliberately set out to put together an anti-rock band, his words."

xref.title: Formation After Sex Pistols Breakup
xref.body: After the Sex Pistols disbanded, Johnny Lydon (formerly Johnny Rotten) chose Jah Wobble to be the bass player for his new group, Public Image Limited. This was a risky choice due to Wobble's prickly personality. "When the Sex Fistals broke up, Johnny Liden turned to Jaw to be the bass player in his new group, Public Image Limited."

xref.title: Johnny Lydon's Previous Band
xref.body: The Sex Pistols were Johnny Lydon's band before he formed Public Image Limited, where he pursued an "anti-rock" direction. "Public Image Limited, Johnny Lydon's band after the Sex Pistols, was also unconventional in its own way."

xref.title: Johnny Lydon's Refusal to Write Lyrics (1990s)
xref.body: During a 1990s reunion, three-quarters of the Sex Pistols recorded music for a potential second album with producer Chris Thomas. They presented these tracks on cassette to Johnny Lydon for him to write lyrics. Lydon refused, stating he was "miffed that he wasn't involved in the writing and the recording of the music," which effectively halted the project. "They then put everything on cassette and then slipped it under the door of Johnny Lydon's room and told him to write some lyrics. Mifft that he wasn't involved in the writing and the recording of the music, he refused, or so he says, and that killed the project in its tracks."

xref.title: Johnny Lydon's Return
xref.body: After the dissolution of Public Image Limited, Johnny Lydon eventually returned to perform with the Sex Pistols. "Johnny ended up back with the Sex Pistols, more on that later, and participated in a variety of other musical projects."

xref.body: This was Johnny Lydon's successful band formed after the Sex Pistols. They had been apart for almost 17 years before Johnny Lydon resurrected the name. "Johnny Lydon's post sex pistols band. They didn't exist for almost 17 years before Johnny resurrected the name."

xref.title: Post-Sex Pistols Experimental Vision
xref.body: After the Sex Pistols, Johnny Lydon formed Public Image Limited (PiL) with the aim of exploring more experimental rock, incorporating influences from reggae, dub, 1970s German rock, and funk musicians. "He was looking for a more experimental way of dealing with rock. He got deep into reggae and dub."

xref.title: Real Name and Nickname Origin
xref.body: Sid Vicious's birth name was John Simon Richie. His friend Johnny Lydon (Johnny Rotten) gave him the nickname "Sid" after Lydon's pet hamster. The "Vicious" part of his name was inspired by a Lou Reed song. Despite being initially "quite a gentle guy," Richie felt compelled to live up to the "Vicious" title.
